text:
maria: FYI, customer ACME reported 401s after their Azure AD rotated keys around 03:10 UTC. Error shows 'invalid signature'. Sending logs.
alex: Can you paste the exact error and the token header? suspect kid mismatch or stale JWKS cache.
maria: Here is the stack we get from the proxy:
```
2026-03-17T03:12:17Z verify_jwt: signature verification failed: token kid=old-kid, jwks lookup returned keys=[old-kid]
error=invalid_signature
```
Also token header:
```
{"alg":"RS256","kid":"new-kid","typ":"JWT"}
```
But our JWKS cache still only contains old-kid.
jonathan: Did the JWKS endpoint return the new key? can you curl it?
maria: curling the customer's JWKS (their idp):
```
curl -sv https://login.microsoftonline.com/tenant123/.well-known/jwks.json
> HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Cache-Control: max-age=3600, public
< Age: 3
{ ... keys: [ { kid: "new-kid" }, { kid: "old-kid" } ] }
```
sasha: So the JWKS endpoint already has new-kid. Our runtime cache must be serving from memory and not refreshing on rotation. Maybe CDN or proxy cached old response earlier with long TTL.
alex: Support says they saw successful rotation at 03:05 and then 5-10mins of spurious 401s. That fits cached JWKS. Two possible causes: (1) our JWKS cache TTL is too long, (2) we don't attempt a fetch on signature failure.
maria: Repro steps I used locally: generate a token with new-kid, then call our verify endpoint which uses cached JWKS -- gets invalid signature. Then a manual flush of JWKS cache (POST /internal/jwks/refresh) makes it work instantly.
jonathan: Good repro. Short-term mitigation: implement aggressive on-demand refresh when a verification fails with kid-not-found or invalid_signature where header.kid not in cached set OR signature fails for a known kid. Also add a small leeway for exp/iat clock skew.
sasha: Agreed. Also ensure we respect Cache-Control and set a hard cap (e.g., 5m) for JWKS memory TTL for third-party IdPs that sometimes misconfigure far-future caches.
alex: Can we also add a fallback to fetch JWKS with cache-busting param (e.g., ?_ts=) if we get a verification failure? Less likely to hit CDN cached old object.
maria: Quick patch we tested in dev: on RS256 verification failure -> attempt one immediate fetch of JWKS, re-verify token once, then fail. PR: https://git.redwood.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/6432 (canary branch jwks-refresh-on-fail)
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary jwks-refresh-on-fail -> eng-runtime-canary at 2026-03-17T09:00:00Z
support-bot: Created internal ticket INF-3421, linked customer case #C-18927, added logs and repro steps.
jonathan: Follow-ups: (1) add metrics: jwks_refresh_on_fail_count, jwks_cache_age_seconds; (2) add test for simultaneous rotation causing N races; (3) update runbook to advise SSO customers to set short jwks ttl on their CDN.
sasha: Also set default verification leeway to 10s and allow config per-tenant.
alex: Rollout plan: canary for 2 hours, monitor 401 rate for affected customer and system-wide increase in jwks refreshes. If everything is green, promote to stable.
maria: Thanks all — I'll notify the customer with mitigation and ETA for full rollout. :thumbsup:
alex: Small note: if idp rotates and accidentally deletes old-kid before tokens expire, we could still see signature fails. We should recommend signing key overlap window in docs.
maria: Good call. I'll add to the SSO onboarding checklist.
